LHX.sentence: L3Harris barely moved, but its profit margins are running lower than the other big defense contractors, and the open question is whether that's a temporary supply-chain hangover or something more lasting — either way, defense spending stays strong.

ASML.sentence: ASML is quiet — the price has cooled slightly, but as the only company on earth making the machines that print the most advanced chips, it's just doing its usual thing.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having a quiet down week — industrial gas demand is steady and they keep nudging prices up, and unusually the market is pricing this best-in-class operator no richer than its rivals.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft ticked up and has been the clear standout among the big tech names lately, with its cloud and AI story just grinding along without drama.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher was flat, but biotech funding is thawing after a long freeze, and that money usually turns into lab-equipment orders a couple of quarters later.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge slipped a touch, but this pipeline toll-road business keeps paying a hefty dividend that now looks generously priced.

NOW.sentence: ServiceNow jumped sharply this week and is still well below its earlier high — big companies and government agencies keep signing on for its AI workflow tools, which are long-term contracts that stick.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore drifted down even as copper prices have been surging, so this miner and trading house looks like it may be lagging a move it should eventually catch up to.

MLM.sentence: Martin Marietta eased back slightly, but the price it gets for a ton of crushed stone is still climbing nicely, which is the part of this quarry business that actually matters.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA slipped a bit — most of its sales are in Mexican pesos, and a strong peso is quietly helping this Latin American Coke bottler.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras had a good day on cooperating oil prices, though its earnings may be near the top of the cycle, which can be a signal to be a little cautious.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk pulled back after a strong run, and while its shipping fleet is technically priced cheaply, the stock had climbed fast enough that it looks stretched for now.

MA.sentence: Mastercard drifted down and, unusually, is priced a shade cheaper than its twin Visa — people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so this is more a mood swing than a business change.

ISRG.sentence: The da Vinci surgical robot maker eased slightly, but hospitals keep doing more procedures on its machines, and each operation sells more of the disposable supplies that drive most of its revenue.
